messages:
incident-bot: :pager: page to @ryan (on-call) — High 5xx spike for tenant `kestrel` on VPC dedicated pool cp-nyc-2. Alert: 5xx rate 22% over baseline, average latency doubled. Auto-fallback observed to 'ephemeral-quant-v1' variants.
ryan: grabbing it. seeing the graph in console, thanks bot.
ryan: quick triage — errors in proxy show 502s with 'kv-cache-miss' followed by worker OOMs. looks like model variant churn is causing cache pressure.
ada: (sorry stepping in) ada here, can you confirm customer impact? SLA tier?
kestrel-sre: Kestrel SRE (on call) — confirmed. Several internal endpoints backpressureing. Production users seeing degraded responses and some timeouts. We're routing traffic via our edge to the VPC. Customer tier: enterprise / dedicated.
ryan: thx. high level plan: 1) apply tenant-level override to pin to a known-safe model version; 2) disable ephemeral fallback for kestrel while we stabilize; 3) route a small % to a canary variant. Need eng-runtime to verify pin behavior. @lex can you eyeball kernel / runtime logs?
lex: on it. pulling runtime logs for cp-nyc-2. early signs: continuous batching queue spiking at 4k requests, kernel swap spikes, and a kernel selection fallback that increases memory footprint (quant->non-quant mix). probably the runtime selected a less-quantized kernel mid-rollout.
lex: recommend pin to `redwood/gpt-lite-3-8b-quant@2026-03-10` (safe quantized build) and set safe_variant to `gpt-lite-3-8b-quant-stable`. That should reduce memory by ~45%.
maria-cs: maria from CS — I'll notify Kestrel PM+SRE that we're applying a controlled pin and will update them when it's stable. Need ETA for recovery.
ryan: ok applying tenant override now. command (internal):
```
POST /internal/tenants/kestrel/overrides
Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "pin_model": "redwood/gpt-lite-3-8b-quant@2026-03-10",
  "safe_variant": "gpt-lite-3-8b-quant-stable",
  "disable_ephemeral_fallback": true,
  "reason": "runtime memory pressure and variant churn causing 5xx",
  "operator": "ryan",
  "expires_at": "2026-03-15T04:00:00Z"
}
```
deploy-bot: override request received, scheduling rollout to kestrel tenant group. estimated propagation ~18s.
ryan: rolling now. watching metrics.
lex: checking runtime logs — override accepted, scheduler pinned model on 3/5 workers in cp-nyc-2 within 12s.
kestrel-sre: seeing a drop in 5xx already. latency trending down. thanks. :white_check_mark:
maria-cs: told customer. they're appreciative we did a quick pin. asked for postmortem and whether we disabled automatic fallbacks (they want explanation).
ada: can we confirm that disabling ephemeral fallback won't cause capacity starvation? we don't want to make things worse.
lex: good question — we set disable_ephemeral_fallback only for kestrel. autoscaler will allow burst up to reserved headroom, but because model memory dropped due to quantized model, effective capacity improved. safe to keep disabled until we finish deeper fix.
ryan: monitoring 5xx window — 1m avg at 2% now, down from 22%. will hold for 30m and then start a gradual re-enable test.
lex: parallel investigation — looking at kernel selection heuristics that picked mixed kernels during a small node GC window. likely race in kernel-matcher: when sequence lengths vary, it can choose a default non-quant kernel. pushing a patch to prefer quant kernel for pinned quant models.
ada: any customer data or request muting? we need to check logs for any dropped requests that might have returned partial responses.
kestrel-sre: we saw some truncated responses logged earlier, but no user data leaked. all logs internal.
ryan: making an incident record: creating INC-2519876543 and assigning to runtime team for postmortem. will tag kestrel contact.
ryan: adding runbook excerpt to the ticket for future similar events:
```
1) If 5xx spike for a dedicated tenant:
  a) check runtime memory and kernel selection logs
  b) apply tenant override pin to last-known stable quant model
  c) disable ephemeral fallback for that tenant only
  d) notify customer and follow up with postmortem
  e) open runtime bug for kernel-matcher heuristic
```
lex: I'll open PR for the kernel-matcher fix and link it to the incident. target ship in next patch window but we'll also hotfix if we see recurrence.
maria-cs: customer asked for a temporary SLA credit calculation — can ops provide duration of impact?
ryan: impact window ~18:21 — 18:43 (22 minutes peak), but degraded for ~35 minutes total. I'll put those numbers in the ticket.
kestrel-sre: confirming no business-critical transactions lost; they requeued and retried downstream.
ada: who will own follow-up: runtime bug + on-call runbook updates?
lex: runtime will own the kernel-matcher bug. ryan/ada please update on-call runbook.
ryan: will do. adding notes: do not re-enable ephemeral fallback globally for kestrel until kernel-matcher fix merged and canary validated.
ryan: planning a gradual rollback test in 1hr: will enable ephemeral fallback for 1% traffic -> 5% -> 20% if 5xx stays below 1%. will communicate each step.
maria-cs: customer prefers a canary window in their low-traffic hours, ok to proceed; schedule locked to their timezone.
lex: final note — internal mitigation applied: pinned to quant build + disabled fallback. runtime patch in progress. please add any other details to the incident ticket.
ryan: thanks everyone. closing active page — will keep thread updated as we run the canary. :lock:
incident-bot: Incident INC-2519876543 created and assigned to runtime. Links: internal INC-2519876543 | runbook excerpt added.
